about: Every provider DipTick knows, compiled into diptick.exe and changed only with DipTick, by hand, from each provider's own pages. Nothing here is fetched over the network. 'checked' is the day the list was read through, and an entry's own 'checked' the day its pages were read again; 'rechecked' is the newest of those.

providers.about: runs open models on this PC; free

providers.name: LM Studio
providers.about: a desktop app that runs open models

providers.name: vLLM

providers.name: text-generation-webui

providers.name: LMDeploy

providers.name: Xinference

providers.name: mistral.rs

providers.name: TabbyAPI

providers.keyHow: the key TabbyAPI makes at first start

providers.about: speech to text on this PC
providers.needs: It does not chat: it turns speech into text through its own /inference request, which DipTick uses with media.speech whispercpp (WAV, FLAC, MP3 and Ogg Vorbis).

providers.name: stable-diffusion.cpp (sd-server)
providers.about: images and video on this PC
providers.needs: It does not chat: it makes images through its OpenAI-shaped /v1/images/generations and video through its own /sdcpp/v1/vid_gen, which DipTick uses with media.images sdcpp and media.video sdcpp.

providers.name: gemma.cpp
providers.about: Google's small engine for Gemma
providers.note: Its API server (gemma_api_server) speaks Google's generateContent; text only.

providers.name: ComfyUI
providers.about: node workflows for images and video
providers.needs: It does not chat: it runs your workflows through its own API (/prompt, /history, /view), which DipTick uses with media.images comfyui and media.video comfyui, filling the workflow's {{prompt}}.

providers.name: OpenAI
providers.about: the GPT models
providers.keepsNote: Not used for training unless you opt in; abuse logs up to 30 days; zero retention by approval.

providers.name: Anthropic

providers.keepsNote: Never used for training without your permission; zero retention by arrangement.

providers.name: Google Gemini API
providers.about: Gemini, Imagen and Veo with a key from Google AI Studio
providers.note: Google's own generateContent, so Gemini 3 and later can search with Google and read pages you name. The key goes in a header, never in an address.
providers.keepsNote: Free use may be read by reviewers and used to improve Google's products; paid use is not, and its logs are kept for a limited time.

providers.name: Mistral AI
providers.about: Mistral's models, from Paris
providers.keepsNote: Kept 30 days for abuse checks unless zero retention is on; not used for training.

providers.name: xAI
providers.about: the Grok models, images and video

providers.keepsNote: Kept 30 days for auditing; never trained on without your permission; zero retention available.

providers.name: DeepSeek
providers.about: DeepSeek's models
providers.keepsNote: Stored in China; may be used for training, with a right to opt out.

providers.name: StepFun

providers.name: Cohere

providers.name: Xiaomi MiMo

providers.name: Groq

providers.keepsNote: Not kept by default; up to 30 days for abuse checks; zero retention in Data Controls.

providers.name: Together AI

providers.keepsNote: Kept by default; switch storage off for zero retention; training use is off unless you opt in.

providers.name: Fireworks AI

providers.about: open models at low prices

providers.keepsNote: Kept to speed up answers unless zero retention is on; never used for training.

providers.name: Novita AI
providers.about: open models and GPUs

providers.name: Baseten

providers.keepsNote: Model APIs keep no inputs or outputs.

providers.name: Cerebras
providers.about: open models on wafer-scale chips

providers.name: SambaNova Cloud
providers.about: open models on its own chips

providers.name: FriendliAI
providers.about: its serverless endpoints for open models
providers.keepsNote: Not shared and not used for training.

providers.name: Featherless
providers.about: thousands of open models for a flat fee
providers.keepsNote: Does not log prompts or completions.

providers.name: Nscale
providers.about: serverless open models
providers.keyHow: a service token from the Nscale console (Settings, Service Tokens), sent as a bearer token
providers.note: Its documentation (docs.nscale.com) gives chat completions with tools, images through /v1/images/generations (media.images nscale, with the model you name), and its models through /v1/models; its model list names vision models too.
providers.keepsNote: Requests are never logged or trained on.

providers.name: Scaleway Generative APIs
providers.about: open models in Europe
providers.keepsNote: Not used for training; usage figures, not content, kept up to 6 months.

providers.name: OVHcloud AI Endpoints
providers.about: open models in Europe
providers.keyHow: OVHcloud Manager: your Public Cloud project, AI & Machine Learning, AI Endpoints
providers.keepsNote: It does not store user data.

providers.name: NVIDIA API catalog
providers.about: models NVIDIA hosts at build.nvidia.com
providers.note: Its terms are for trial use, not production.

providers.name: Chutes
providers.about: serverless open models, some in trusted hardware
providers.keyHow: an API key (cpk_...) from the Chutes dashboard or its CLI
providers.keepsNote: Public models: prompts and outputs are not logged.

providers.name: SiliconFlow
providers.about: open models and image models

providers.name: Vultr Serverless Inference
providers.about: open models on Vultr's cloud
providers.keyHow: a key from the Vultr Cloud Inference console
providers.note: Its model list lives at /v1/chat/models, not /v1/models.
providers.keepsNote: Inference data is not used for training.

providers.name: RunPod Serverless
providers.about: your own vLLM endpoint on RunPod
providers.keyHow: RUNPOD_API_KEY from the RunPod console

providers.name: Modal
providers.about: a model server you deploy on Modal
providers.keyHow: whatever your deployment asks; Modal's vLLM example asks none
providers.keepsNote: Inference endpoints write no payloads; function data is deleted within 7 days.

providers.name: Ollama Cloud
providers.about: Ollama's hosted models
providers.keepsNote: Not used to train models.

providers.name: fal (OpenRouter router)
providers.about: chat models through fal's OpenRouter router
providers.keyHow: FAL_KEY from your fal dashboard
providers.note: fal sends its key as 'Authorization: Key', and DipTick does the same for it. Its image and video models go through its own queue API (queue.fal.run), with media.images fal or media.video fal and the model you name; the key goes only to fal's own hosts.
providers.keepsNote: Inputs and outputs are stored by default so they can be fetched later.

providers.name: Replicate
providers.about: thousands of models, many of them for images and video
providers.needs: It does not chat: Replicate "does not offer an OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint". Its predictions API makes images and video, which DipTick uses with media.images replicate or media.video replicate and the model you name (owner/name).
providers.keepsNote: API inputs and outputs are removed after an hour.

providers.name: WaveSpeedAI
providers.about: image and video models
providers.needs: It does not chat: it makes images and video through its own API, which DipTick uses with media.images wavespeed or media.video wavespeed and the model you name (like wavespeed-ai/flux-dev).
providers.keepsNote: Outputs are deleted after 7 days; prompts are not kept long, and outputs are not used for training.

providers.name: Inferless
providers.about: serverless GPUs for your own models
providers.keyHow: a workspace API key from Inferless's settings (Workspace API keys), sent as a bearer token
providers.note: Give the model's own inference address, as its API tab shows it (…/v2/models/<model>/versions/1/infer). DipTick sends one prompt, in the input 'prompt', and reads the answer from 'generated_text' or the first text output, as Inferless's own templates do; no tools, no files. Its team joined Baseten on 2026-03-09, with no word on the platform's future.
providers.keepsNote: Not documented: it runs your own deployment of your own model.

providers.name: Azure OpenAI (Microsoft Foundry)
providers.about: OpenAI's and other makers' models in your Azure resource
providers.keyHow: your resource's key, shown with your deployment in the Foundry portal
providers.note: The model is your deployment's name. Microsoft recommends its Responses API for OpenAI's models; Chat Completions still answers.
providers.keepsNote: Kept 30 days for abuse checks unless modified monitoring is approved; not used for training.

providers.name: Claude in Microsoft Foundry
providers.about: Claude through your Azure resource, billed by Azure
providers.keyHow: the Key on your deployment's Details tab in the Foundry portal
providers.note: The model is your deployment's name; by default it matches the model's ID.
providers.keepsNote: Anthropic's data use terms apply; deployments hosted on Azure keep prompts within Azure.

providers.name: Amazon Bedrock
providers.about: open-weight models on AWS, with a Bedrock API key
providers.note: Through Bedrock's OpenAI-compatible Mantle endpoint, which lists its models; Claude on Bedrock is its own entry.
providers.keepsNote: Prompts and completions are not stored or logged, and not used for training.

providers.name: Claude in Amazon Bedrock
providers.about: Claude on AWS-run servers, billed by AWS
providers.keyHow: a short-term Bedrock bearer token (aws-bedrock-token-generator), 12 hours at most
providers.note: Bedrock has no web search, structured outputs or server-side fallback for Claude.
providers.keepsNote: Governed by Amazon Bedrock: prompts and completions are not stored or used for training.

providers.name: Claude Platform on AWS
providers.about: Anthropic's own platform, billed through AWS Marketplace
providers.keyHow: AWS Console: Claude Platform on AWS, API keys; and your workspace ID (wrkspc_...)
providers.note: Every call names your workspace: set its workspace setting to your wrkspc_ ID.
providers.keepsNote: Anthropic processes and stores it, on AWS.

providers.name: Google Cloud Vertex AI
providers.about: Gemini and the open models Google hosts, in your Google Cloud project
providers.keyHow: your Google Cloud sign-in: 'gcloud auth application-default login', or GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS naming a service account's key file
providers.note: Google now calls it the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. Models are named like google/gemini-3.5-flash. Its tokens last an hour; DipTick renews them.
providers.keepsNote: Gemini caches inputs up to 24 hours unless caching is switched off; prompts may be logged for abuse checks.

providers.name: Claude on Google Cloud
providers.about: Claude in your Google Cloud project, billed by Google
providers.keyHow: your Google Cloud sign-in: 'gcloud auth application-default login', or GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS naming a service account's key file
providers.note: Location global is Anthropic's recommendation; us and eu keep traffic in one area; single regions serve Sonnet 4.6 and older.
providers.keepsNote: Governed by Google Cloud.

providers.name: Vertex AI express mode
providers.about: Vertex AI with an API key instead of a sign-in
providers.keyHow: the API key from APIs & Services, Credentials, in the Google Cloud console in express mode
providers.note: Google's generateContent at the global address, with the key in a header (Google's own example puts it in the address, which DipTick never does). Gemini 3 and later can search with Google.

providers.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
providers.about: open models on Cloudflare's network
providers.keepsNote: Not used for training; not stored unless you use one of its storage services.

providers.name: Databricks
providers.about: models served in your Databricks workspace
providers.keyHow: a Databricks token (dapi-...)
providers.keepsNote: Not used for training; may be held a while for abuse checks.

providers.name: DigitalOcean Serverless Inference
providers.about: open and commercial models on DigitalOcean
providers.keyHow: a model access key from the DigitalOcean Control Panel
providers.keepsNote: It does not store inputs or outputs.

providers.name: Heroku Managed Inference
providers.about: models attached to a Heroku app
providers.keyHow: the add-on's INFERENCE_KEY config var
providers.note: Its region is the start of the add-on's INFERENCE_URL: us or eu.
providers.keepsNote: Prompts are not stored, logged or used for training.

providers.name: Snowflake Cortex
providers.about: models inside your Snowflake account
providers.keyHow: a Snowflake programmatic access token
providers.keepsNote: Runs inside Snowflake; not used to train models for others.

providers.name: Oracle OCI Generative AI
providers.about: models in your Oracle Cloud tenancy
providers.keepsNote: Inference inputs and outputs are not stored.

providers.name: IBM watsonx.ai model gateway
providers.about: the providers you connect to watsonx, behind one address
providers.keyHow: an IBM Cloud API key
providers.note: In preview; connect its providers in watsonx first.
providers.keepsNote: Stateless: prompts are not stored.

providers.name: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (Qwen)
providers.about: the Qwen models and others
providers.note: Its address depends on the region: dashscope-us.aliyuncs.com for the US, <workspace>.ap-southeast-1.maas.aliyuncs.com for Singapore, <workspace>.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com for Beijing.
providers.keepsNote: Never used for model training.

providers.name: Tencent Cloud TokenHub
providers.about: Hunyuan, DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax and MiMo behind one key
providers.keepsNote: Tencent Cloud's privacy policy and data processing agreement apply.

providers.name: Tencent Hunyuan
providers.about: the Hunyuan models, on Tencent Cloud in China
providers.note: Tencent is moving Hunyuan to TokenHub; this platform adds no new models.

providers.name: Baidu Qianfan
providers.about: the ERNIE models and others, on Baidu AI Cloud

providers.name: Volcengine Ark (Doubao)
providers.about: ByteDance's Doubao models, in China
providers.keepsNote: What you send is kept and used to improve its models only through an endpoint you opt into its Collaboration Reward Program (for free tokens, and for good once used); otherwise, its page says, it is neither collected nor stored.

providers.name: BytePlus ModelArk
providers.about: ByteDance's Seed, Seedream and Seedance models, outside China
providers.keyHow: an API key from the ModelArk console
providers.keepsNote: Not used for its own training without your authorization.

providers.name: OpenRouter
providers.about: hundreds of models from many makers, one key
providers.keepsNote: Prompts are not stored unless you opt in; the provider behind each answer keeps by its own rules.

providers.name: Vercel AI Gateway
providers.about: models from many makers through Vercel, one key
providers.keepsNote: Zero retention at the gateway by default; the provider behind each answer keeps by its own rules.

providers.name: Hugging Face Inference Providers
providers.about: open models from many hosts, one Hugging Face token
providers.note: The token needs the permission 'Make calls to Inference Providers'. A model name can end in :fastest, :cheapest or :<provider>.
providers.keepsNote: Request bodies are not stored; logs without user data kept up to 30 days; each host keeps by its own rules.

providers.name: LiteLLM proxy
providers.about: your own gateway in front of any providers
providers.keyHow: a virtual key from your proxy, if it asks for one
providers.keepsNote: Your own proxy; the providers behind it keep by their own rules.
